text:
The Devils come home Thursday with a five-game winning streak behind them and a loss in front of them: they fell 4-2 at WPG two days ago, ending the run. They're 4-1-0 in their last five and without Anthony Mantha (neck), whose minutes are going to Connor Brown (17:37 a night, up from 14:26) and Cody Glass. WSH won 3-2 at OTT on Cole Hutson's overtime goal, is 3-2-0 over its last five, and is missing Vincent Desharnais. NJD sits second in the Metropolitan, six points ahead of fourth-place WSH, and the Capitals won the first meeting 4-2 on Oct 17, though the Devils deserved it more (73% of simulated replays).

Our model has NJD ahead 3.41 expected goals to 2.89 (expected goals measure the quality of chances). The Devils have taken 58% of them at five on five, against 53% for WSH, and they allow 2.56 per 60 minutes to WSH's 3.39. The special-teams matchup to watch: NJD's power play creates 0.81 expected goals a game, and WSH's penalty kill allows 0.86. WSH takes 4.3 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Connor Hellebuyck (+1.5 goals saved above expected, a measure of saves beyond what the shot quality called for) and Logan Thompson (+2.7) are both positive. Thompson was +28.2 last season to Hellebuyck's +3.4.

Jack Hughes is our top pick, with a 42% chance to score and an 81% chance at a point, riding a six-game point streak. Jesper Bratt has the same streak and nine points in five games against WSH. Alex Tuch is the Capitals' best bet at 36% to score, while Tom Wilson and Alex Ovechkin, each at 21%, are both overdue: no goals in twelve and eleven games.
